record.metric: Reuters documented military-relevant procurement entities and import records
record.observed_state: Reuters documented over 5,000 MOD-linked procurement agencies and at least $2 billion of imported equipment since January 2025. The reported import records are source-defined; no separate additive total is assigned to any MOD unit.

record.metric: QatarEnergy contracted LNG purchases, million metric tons per annum
record.observed_state: QatarEnergy reported about 7 million metric tons per year of purchased LNG under long-term agreements, alongside an estimated three-year repair horizon for two damaged Ras Laffan trains.

events.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed a ballistic missile struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and caused a fire. Saudi authorities had not confirmed the reported strike in Reuters' October 27 account.

The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting three ballistic missiles toward Saudi Arabia's Eastern Region and four drones toward its Southern Region. Civil Defense separately issued and cleared regional alerts.
Qatari mediators presented a proposed war-ending arrangement to Iran. A senior Iranian official said the ideas on offer were unacceptable; no agreement was announced.

Reuters identified a network of more than 5,000 Iranian Defense Ministry-associated procurement agencies and traced at least $2 billion in imported military-relevant equipment since January 2025 from banking, company and shipping records.
QatarEnergy CEO Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi said the company signed long-term purchases totaling about seven million metric tons of LNG annually, including contracts involving Woodside and Cheniere.
QatarEnergy's chief executive said damage to two Ras Laffan LNG production trains would take around three years to repair. The reported purchase contracts serve future supply periods.
